newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium price spike likely - Bird.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium price spike likely - Bird.

text.p: The aluminium market's tight supply-demand balance following the depressed prices of late-1996, will lead to a period of very high prices, according to industry specialists Anthony Bird and Associates.
In its latest quarterly analysis Bird said that aluminium supply was almost in complete balance with demand in 1996.
"But even though idled capacity is now being quietly recommissioned, supply continues to run behind demand, and there will be a deficit of about 0.4 million tonnes this year," Bird said.
Previous experience suggested that in boom conditions actual prices could go as much as 80 percent above trend. This happened in early 1988 and late 1999 was expected to be similar, Bird said.
"Thus a price spike is coming. But we do not expect it to last. By 1999 high prices will start to hurt aluminium's competitive position quite badly and put a brake on demand growth," the report said.
